page: Microsoft Azure E32bds_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EBDSv5 family, powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 1229 GB, and the instance supports premium block storage.

Benchmark data shows average performance across most compute and memory metrics. The Passmark memory score is a notable highlight, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 2815.31. In contrast, CPU-bound tasks such as stress-ng single-core (1899.28) and multi-core (31078.76) fall into the middle 50% tier. Large-block memory write bandwidth reaches 69.57 GB/sec, while read-only small-block cached memory bandwidth is recorded at 1669.69 GB/sec.

For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong text generation performance on small (135M) language models at 269.82 tokens/sec. However, it exhibits a clear performance tradeoff on larger models, with prompt processing for a 70B model dropping to a weak 6.63 tokens/sec. Given the 256 GB memory capacity, bundled 1229 GB local storage, and average database operation scores (15356.14 on Passmark), this server is suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, and caching layers such as Redis, where it handles 31.6 million SET operations per second.
description: Microsoft Azure E32bds_v5 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server from the EBDSv5 family, featuring a dedicated 32-vCPU Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per core resource density, alongside 1229 GB of local storage. Performance benchmarks generally fall within the average range, including a Passmark CPU score of 36975.23 and a static web serving throughput of 34.04 GB/sec. However, its memory subsystem performs strongly, with a Passmark memory score in the top 25%. While it handles small-model LLM text generation efficiently, it struggles with larger 70B models, showing a clear tradeoff in compute-heavy AI tasks. This server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching applications.
